explanation: In modern C++, smart pointers such as std::unique_ptr are used to manage dynamic memory automatically, ensuring proper resource deallocation and preventing memory leaks. Unlike raw pointers, std::unique_ptr enforces exclusive ownership of the resource, providing a safer and more expressive way to handle dynamic objects within the scope of RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization). This promotes safer code by automating memory management and reducing the risk of dangling pointers.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of std::unique_ptr to manage a dynamically allocated Widget object. It shows how to create a unique_ptr using std::make_unique, how ownership can be transferred via std::move, and how the resource is automatically cleaned up when the unique_ptr goes out of scope. This exemplifies modern C++'s RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) idiom, ensuring safe and exception-resistant memory management.
